faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (adswizz vergibt je Abruf eine listeningSessionID, AIS leitet ueber hash_redirect um, Last-Modified liegt nur 0 s vor dem Abruf, Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst simplecastaudio.com) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: Sean Hayes discusses health habits, Broadway endurance, and sitcoms on Staying Alive.
kurzfassung: Sean Hayes joins Jon Gabrus and Adam Pally to discuss his notoriously unhealthy diet and recent wake-up call regarding his blood work. The conversation covers the physical toll of starring in a Broadway two-hander and the unique pace of working on multi-cam sitcoms. They also touch upon memorization techniques, recurring stage anxiety dreams, and the struggle to find lifestyle balance.
stichpunkte: Sean Hayes reveals that poor blood work results forced him to finally reconsider a lifelong diet consisting heavily of sugar and ice cream.
The hosts and guest compare the physical demands of performing eight shows a week on Broadway to professional athletics.
Hayes discusses the chaotic yet efficient schedule of multi-camera sitcoms, contrasting it with single-cam productions.
The conversation delves into methods for memorizing heavy dialogue, comparing writing lines down to treating scripts like songs.
Hayes shares a recurring nightmare about being unprepared backstage in a theater and forgetting his lines.
The group touches upon modern weight-loss medications and the psychological shift of finally feeling satiated after a meal.
Reflecting on past projects, Hayes recalls hosting the short-lived salon-based game show Hair Jacked.

clips.text: A young fan wearing foam clogs approached the actor after a Broadway performance and asked for an autograph on his footwear.

clips.hook: They check the receipt from last night.
clips.text: The demanding schedule of a theatrical run supposedly requires actors to maintain high-calorie late-night dining habits just to survive.

clips.hook: God bless, I play Larry, too.
clips.text: During a one-man theatrical performance, the actor briefly caught himself waiting on stage for another character to speak before realizing he portrayed every single role.
Anxious moments before going on stage for a solo show frequently involved relieving digestive pressure right as the stage manager checked in.
